Maria: Quick question about payments API error behavior. Mobile clients sometimes send unknown enum values and we currently return 400. Should clients ever retry or is that always a non-retryable 4xx?
Devon: If it's a client-side validation problem (unknown enum, missing required), treat as 4xx and do not auto-retry. 4xx = fix request. :white_check_mark:
Kai: We have been a bit inconsistent: 400 generic, 422 for semantic issues, 409 for conflicts. We should pick a clear mapping for schema evolution cases.
Andrea: Suggestion: try to be forgiving when possible. If server can map unknown enum to an INTERNAL default (e.g., OTHER) and continue, do that. Only 4xx if processing truly cannot proceed.
Samir: Example: mobile v1 sent currency: "XBT" (we support USD/EUR). Service returned 400 and UI surfaced an error. If downstream can assume account currency, better to accept and log. If currency is critical for routing, 4xx is valid.
Maria: So two dimensions: validation vs processing-blocking incompatibility. Validation errors -> 4xx non-retryable. Transient infra/load -> 5xx or 429 -> retryable.
Devon: Concrete mapping proposal:
- 400/422 -> client input error -> DO NOT RETRY
- 409 -> state conflict -> handle specially, maybe retry after reconciliation
- 429 -> rate limit -> retry with backoff
- 5xx (502/503/504) -> transient server error -> retry with exponential backoff
opsbot: deploybot: payments-service v2.3.2 deployed to prod :rocket:
Kai: Idea: add optional top-level `error.retryable: boolean` in responses so SDKs can make deterministic decisions. Default false for 4xx.
Andrea: I like `error.code` + `error.retryable`. Example response idea:
```
{
  \"error\": {
    \"code\": \"invalid_currency\",
    \"message\": \"currency 'XBT' not supported\",
    \"retryable\": false
  }
}
```
Samir: Note: adding `retryable` later should be non-breaking. Servers can add it and older SDKs ignore it. SDKs that understand it can take advantage.
Maria: Priority for SDK logic should be: HTTP status -> presence of `error.retryable` -> SDK policy. That covers coarse + fine-grain.
Devon: Agree. Also guardrails: if status is 503 but `error.retryable:false`, SDK should not retry. That lets us mark certain failures as non-retryable even if status is 5xx.
Kai: About narrowing enums: we should provide a deprecation header before returning hard 4xx. Proposal: `X-Param-Deprecation: name='currency'; will-enforce='2026-05-01'; notice-days=30` or similar. We should document windows: 30d for behavioral changes, 60d for removals.
Andrea: +1. We'll include header semantics and example text in API contract doc.
Samir: Action items:
- update payments API spec to include `error.retryable` examples and header guidance — @Andrea
- SDK change: implement HTTP -> `error.retryable` -> retry/backoff logic — @Maria
- service lint rule: try to accept unknown enums when safe or emit deprecation header before 4xx — @Kai
Maria: I'll add unit tests in sdk-retry: 429/5xx => retryable, 400/422 => non-retryable, and a test where body.error.retryable overrides status.
Devon: Suggested SDK snippet for reference:
```
if (status >= 500 || status == 429) { retry(); }
else if (body.error && body.error.retryable) { retry(); }
else { fail(); }
```
Andrea: Note in docs: do not retry on 4xx even if message sounds transient unless `error.retryable:true`.
Kai: I'll open a PR to update API contract with headers + enum guidance and link it here when ready.
Andrea: One more question: streaming endpoints that terminate mid-stream — should clients retry the stream? Resume with cursor if supported, otherwise treat as transient and restart from beginning.
Samir: We prefer resumable streams with continuation tokens; if not available, full restart as a transient retry.
Maria: Ok, I'll land changes in payments-api-spec and sdk-retry today unless objections. :+1:
Kai: No objections, ping me for review. :eyes:
Andrea: I'll draft deprecation header wording and add examples.
Maria: Closing thread in a few hours if no further comments. :wave:
